subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ with n < P. Let T_j (j ∈ ℕ) and T be currents in 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) (GeometricCurrentOn univ n) such that every T_j is integer multiplicity (IsIntegerMultiplicity), ∂T_j = 0 for every j (contract BoundaryVanishes; vacuous for n = 0), sup_j M(T_j) < ∞ (M = mass = M_{ℝ^P}), and T_j ⇀ T in ℝ^P (WeaklyConvergesOn). Source: Simon Ch. 6, Theorem 8.2 and its printed proof (chapter-06.txt lines 2303–2473, printed pp. 176–179), in the case ∂T_j = 0 singled out by Remark 6.4 (lines 1999–2001) and Remark 8.3(2), with U = ℝ^P. This is the result cited in step 4 of the parent proof, where it is applied to the cycles ∂Q_k.
Book results used:
- Ch. 1: 3.3 (density comparison, chapter-01.txt line 602); 3.12 with Remark 3.11(3) (Besicovitch covering, lines 773–858); 4.4 (Urysohn) and 4.16 (compactness of Radon measures, line 1750).
- Ch. 2: 2.6 (BV compactness, chapter-02.txt line 598).
- Ch. 6: 2.7–2.9 (T = ξ_T μ_T and T⌞A, lines 271–293); 2.14 (lower semicontinuity of M_W); 2.23–2.24 (push-forward); 2.26–2.27 and 2.30–2.31 (cone and its mass bound, lines 452–545); 2.35 (top-dimensional currents with locally finite boundary mass are BV functions, lines 606–639); 3.2(3) and 3.9 (mass and Lipschitz push-forward of IM currents, lines 755–862); 4.4–4.5 and 4.6–4.9 (slices, lines 1223–1374); 5.3 and 6.1 (isoperimetric theorem, with the support bound of its proof, lines 1461–1490 and 1939–1961); 8.1 (Rectifiability Theorem, lines 2155–2296), with the blow-up identities (11)–(13) of its proof.
Sibling used: im_calculus (cmc_imRep_locality_restrict_sub), parts (b) (restriction of an IM current to a Borel set) and (d) (orientation bound).
Departure. The T_j are cycles with sup_j M(T_j) < ∞, so the printed reductions to spt T_j ⊆ K and to ∂T = 0 (Remark 8.3(1)) are not needed. Every step below is local or uses only the global mass bound.
Errata and completions:
- (E1) The isoperimetric fillings in (4) must lie in balls of radius comparable to the balls they fill. The proof of 6.1 via 5.3 gives this support bound. It supplies the radius factor in the cone estimate after (5); the OCR prints '|(S_j − T⌞B_j)(ω)| ≤ cM(S_j − T⌞B_j)|dω|' without it.
- (E2) The constant in (4) is c·γ^{1/(n−1)}; the OCR drops the power.
- (E3) The covering result cited as '??(2) of Ch. 1' is the Besicovitch covering lemma 3.12, in the form of Remark 3.11(3).
- (E4) Footnote 5 (n = 1): an IM 0-current of mass < 1 is zero, so S_r := 0.
- (E5) The selection after (7) ('justified by 4.5(1) and a selection argument') is carried out in full in steps 7–8. The uniform rescaled mass bounds come from a weak limit μ of the mass measures μ_{T_j} and from Θ^{*n}(μ, x) < ∞ at H^n-a.e. x (Ch. 1, 3.3). Bounds for T alone would not do, since weak convergence permits cancellation. The truncation level δ is chosen so that a weak limit ν of the mass measures of the rescaled approximants does not charge {d = δ}, and the convergence of the truncated currents is then proved (step 8(h)).
Notation:
- IM = integer multiplicity; M = mass; M_W = mass in the open set W; ‖ω‖ := sup_x|ω(x)| (Euclidean coefficient norm), finite for test forms.
- (ME) Mass estimate. If spt ω ⊆ W with W open, then |X(ω)| ≤ ‖ω‖·M_W(X). Apply the definition of M_W to ±ω/‖ω‖; if ‖ω‖ = 0 then ω = 0.
- Mass measures (2.7–2.9). If M_W(X) < ∞ for every bounded open W, μ_X is the Radon measure with μ_X(W) = M_W(X) for open W, and X(ω) = ∫⟨ω, ξ_X⟩dμ_X with |ξ_X| = 1 μ_X-a.e. For Borel A, X⌞A(ω) := ∫_A⟨ω, ξ_X⟩dμ_X. So |X⌞A(ω)| ≤ ‖ω‖μ_X(A ∩ spt ω) and μ_{X⌞A} = μ_X⌞A. For IM X = τ(M, θ, ξ) we have μ_X = θH^n⌞M (3.2(3)), ξ_X = ξ μ_X-a.e. (|ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| by im_calculus (d)), and X⌞A is the current represented by (M ∩ A, θ, ξ), which is IM (im_calculus (b)).
- (W) Let λ_i → λ weakly as Radon measures, i.e. ∫f dλ_i → ∫f dλ for f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P). Then limsup_iλ_i(K) ≤ λ(K) for compact K, and λ(V) ≤ liminf_iλ_i(V) for open V. Proof: for compact K ⊆ V open take f ∈ C_c(V; [0, 1]) with f = 1 on K (Ch. 1, 4.4). Then λ_i(K) ≤ ∫f dλ_i → ∫f dλ ≤ λ(V); let V ↓ K (outer regularity). Also λ_i(V) ≥ ∫f dλ_i → ∫f dλ ≥ λ(K); let K ↑ V (inner regularity).
- ω_n := L^n(B^n_1); Θ^{*n}(λ, x) := limsup_{ρ↓0}λ(B_ρ(x))/(ω_nρ^n); η_{x,λ}(y) := λ^{−1}(y − x).
We prove by induction on n the statement CL(n): for every P > n, every sequence of IM T_j ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with ∂T_j = 0 (if n ≥ 1), sup_jM(T_j) < ∞ and T_j ⇀ T has an IM limit T. Passing to a subsequence changes neither the hypotheses nor the conclusion; we do so freely.

1. (n = 0.)
 (a) An IM 0-current X of finite mass has finite carrier, because H⁰ is counting measure, θ ≥ 1 and M(X) = Σθ (3.2(3)). So X = Σ_{i=1}^{N}ε_iδ_{x_i}, with points listed with multiplicity, ε_i = ±1 and N = M(X).
 (b) Let Λ := sup_jM(T_j) and T_j = Σ_{i=1}^{N_j}ε_{j,i}δ_{x_{j,i}} with N_j ≤ Λ. Pass to a subsequence with N_j = N and ε_{j,i} = ε_i for all j, and such that for each i either x_{j,i} → y_i or |x_{j,i}| → ∞. Let I be the set of i of the first kind.
 (c) For a smooth compactly supported function a, T(a) = lim_jΣ_iε_ia(x_{j,i}) = Σ_{i∈I}ε_ia(y_i). So T = Σ_ym(y)δ_y with m(y) := Σ_{i∈I, y_i = y}ε_i ∈ ℤ.
 (d) With F := {m ≠ 0} (finite), T = τ(F, |m|, sign m). F is Borel and countably 0-rectifiable. The multiplicity is a positive integer on F and locally integrable. At each point of F the approximate tangent space is {0}, since the blow-ups of F converge to the single point 0; the orientation is ±1. So T is IM.
2. (Inductive step: set-up.) Let 1 ≤ n < P and assume CL(n − 1); note n − 1 < P. Let T_j, T be as in CL(n) and Λ := sup_jM(T_j) < ∞.
 (a) By 2.14 (SimonGMT WeaklyConvergesOn.massOn_le_liminf), M(T) ≤ liminf_jM(T_j) ≤ Λ. Also ∂T(η) = T(dη) = lim_jT_j(dη) = 0. So T is a cycle of finite mass, T = ξ_Tμ_T and μ_T(ℝ^P) ≤ Λ.
 (b) μ_j := μ_{T_j} = θ_jH^n⌞M_j satisfies μ_j(ℝ^P) = M(T_j) ≤ Λ. By Ch. 1, 4.16, after passing to a subsequence, μ_j → μ weakly for a Radon measure μ. By (W) with V = ℝ^P, μ(ℝ^P) ≤ Λ.
 (c) μ_T ≤ μ. Let K be compact, r > 0 and V := {y : dist(y, K) < r}. By 2.14 and (W), μ_T(K) ≤ μ_T(V) = M_V(T) ≤ liminf_jM_V(T_j) = liminf_jμ_j(V) ≤ limsup_jμ_j(V̄) ≤ μ(V̄). Letting r ↓ 0 gives μ_T(K) ≤ μ(K). By inner regularity, μ_T(A) ≤ μ(A) for every Borel A.
3. (Slices of T are IM; printed (1)–(2).) Fix ξ₀ ∈ ℝ^P, f := |· − ξ₀| (Lip f = 1) and the nondecreasing function F(r) := μ_T(B_r(ξ₀)).
 (a) Fix j. T_j is IM with ∂T_j = 0, so by 4.4–4.5, for a.e. r > 0 the slice ⟨T_j, f, r⟩ is IM and equals ∂(T_j⌞B_r(ξ₀)) (4.5(2)). Moreover ∫_0^∞M(⟨T_j, f, r⟩)dr ≤ M(T_j) ≤ Λ (4.5(1)). As there are countably many j, there is a null set N₁ ⊂ (0, ∞) off which this holds for every j. By Fatou (the functions r ↦ M(⟨T_j, f, r⟩) are L¹-measurable, being the coarea integrands of 4.1 and 4.5(1)), ∫_0^∞liminf_jM(∂(T_j⌞B_r(ξ₀)))dr ≤ Λ, so liminf_jM(∂(T_j⌞B_r(ξ₀))) < ∞ off a null set N₂.
 (b) The spheres ∂B_r(ξ₀), r > 0, are pairwise disjoint and μ is finite. So μ(∂B_r(ξ₀)) = 0 for r off a countable set N₃, and then μ_T(∂B_r(ξ₀)) = 0 by 2(c).

10. (Conclusion.) By steps 7–9, θ(x) is a positive integer for every x ∈ G, hence for H^n-a.e. x ∈ M. Choose a Borel set M′ ⊆ G with H^n(M ∖ M′) = 0; this is possible since H^n is Borel regular and H^n⌞M is σ-finite. Shrinking M′ by an H^n-null Borel set, we may assume that θ agrees on M′ with a Borel function and that ξ(x) orients T_xM for every x ∈ M′.
 - mult := θ on M′ and 0 elsewhere is Borel, ℕ-valued and ≥ 1 on M′. It is locally H^n-integrable, since ∫_{M′}θ dH^n ≤ μ_T(ℝ^P) = M(T) < ∞.
 - orient := ξ is a.e. strongly measurable for H^n⌞M′.
 - M′ ⊆ M is countably n-rectifiable. Removing an H^n-null set changes no blow-up integral ∫_{η_{x,r}(·)}f dH^n, so M′ has approximate tangent space T_xM at H^n-a.e. x ∈ M′, oriented by ξ(x).
 Hence (M′, mult, ξ) is an IMRep in ℝ^P, and T(ω) = ∫_Mθ⟨ω, ξ⟩dH^n = ∫_{M′}mult·ξ(ω)dH^n for every ω. So T is IM. This proves CL(n), and by induction the statement. ∎
proof_key_steps: Induction on the degree: CL(0) holds because bounded-mass IM 0-currents are finite signed sums of point masses, and the bounded points converge.

Pass to μ_{T_j} → μ (Ch. 1, 4.16); μ_T ≤ μ. Slices ∂(T⌞B_r(ξ₀)) are IM for a.e. r: the slices of the T_j are IM with liminf-bounded mass (4.5, Fatou), μ(∂B_r) = 0 makes the restrictions converge, and CL(n − 1) applies (printed (1)–(2)).
Where Θ^{*n}(μ_T, ·) < γ, radii with small (F^{1/n})′ give IM fillings S_r with M(S_r) ≤ μ_T(B_r)/2 in comparable balls (6.1 with the support bound of 5.3); for n = 1 the slice vanishes.
Besicovitch covering, the cone estimate and lower semicontinuity give μ_T{Θ^{*n} < γ} = 0; the Rectifiability Theorem 8.1 gives T = τ(M, θ, ξ) with real θ.
At H^n-a.e. x ∈ M the blow-ups of T converge to θ(x)[[T_xM]] and Θ^{*n}(μ, x) < ∞ (Ch. 1, 3.3); the latter bounds μ_{η_{x,λ#}T_j}(B̄_2(0)) uniformly for j ≥ J(λ).

Diagonal selection on a countable dense family of test forms gives IM cycles X_i ⇀ θ(x)[[T_xM]] with uniform mass bounds. A weak limit ν of their mass measures and Fatou on 4.5(1) give a level δ with IM slices of bounded mass and ν{d = δ} = 0, which proves X_i⌞{d < δ} ⇀ θ(x)[[T_xM]].
Projecting to T_xM gives integer-valued BV functions with uniform bounds (3.9, 2.35); BV compactness and identification of the limit force θ(x) ∈ ℤ, and a Borel modification gives an IMRep of T.

subproblems.title: Integer density, layer decomposition and truncation bounds for a compactly supported top-dimensional integer multiplicity current (Simon 6.3.14 first step and (3)–(7), 2.35, 3.15)
subproblems.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ and let R ∈ 𝒟_{n+1}(ℝ^{n+1}) be integer multiplicity with compact support. Then there are Borel sets U_j ⊆ ℝ^{n+1} (j ∈ ℤ) with U_{j+1} ⊆ U_j, and currents X_j ∈ 𝒟_{n+1}(ℝ^{n+1}) with X_j(ω) = ∫_{U_j} ω(x)(e_0, …, e_n) dL^{n+1}(x) for every ω (X_j = [[U_j]]), such that: (i) for every η ∈ 𝒟^n(ℝ^{n+1}) the family (∂X_j(η))_{j∈ℤ} is summable with sum ∂R(η) (HasSum); (ii) M(∂X_j) ≤ M(∂R) for every j; (iii) for every N ∈ ℕ and every Y ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^{n+1}) with Y(η) = Σ_{j=−N}^{N} ∂X_j(η) for all η, M(Y) ≤ M(∂R). Here M = mass = M_{ℝ^{n+1}} in [0, ∞].

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, proof of 3.14: its first paragraph and (1) (chapter-06.txt lines 1030–1048), (3)–(7) (lines 1048–1105), Remark 3.15 (lines 953–1029) and Remark 2.35 (lines 606–639); the mollification Lemma Ch. 2, 2.5. These are steps 5–7 of the parent proof, for U = ℝ^{n+1}. Part A is the first step of 3.14 (R is given by an integer density); Part B is the layer decomposition and Simon's smoothing estimates (5)–(7).
Siblings used: vanish_off_support (dtc_vanish_off_support), in step A5; mollify_variation (codim1_rdo_dg_sp_mollify_variation), in step B6.
Notation: e = (e_0, …, e_n) is the standard basis (e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1), L = L^{n+1} = volume, H^{n+1} = μHE[n+1] and div φ = trace Dφ. For an n-covector α write α_î := α(e_{i.succAbove 0}, …, e_{i.succAbove(n−1)}), i.e. e with e_i omitted.
Hodge correspondence (Simon 3.15, 2.35). For a vector field φ let ⋆φ be the n-form (⋆φ)(x)(v_0, …, v_{n−1}) := det[φ(x), v_0, …, v_{n−1}]. For an n-form η let φ_η be the vector field with components φ_η^i := (−1)^iη(·)_î. Then:
 (S1) (⋆φ)(x)_î = (−1)^iφ^i(x) (Laplace expansion along the first column). So φ_{⋆φ} = φ and ⋆φ_η = η, since an n-covector on ℝ^{n+1} is determined by its n + 1 values α_î.
 (S2) |(⋆φ)(x)| = |φ(x)|, because the Euclidean coefficient norm of α is (Σ_iα_î²)^{1/2}.
 (S3) For a C¹ n-form η, dη(x)(e) = Σ_i(−1)^i∂_i(η(·)_î)(x) = div φ_η(x) (Mathlib extDeriv_apply).
 (S4) η is a test form iff φ_η is C^∞ with compact support.
 (S5) ∫div φ dL = 0 for C¹ compactly supported φ (fundamental theorem of calculus in each coordinate).
Part A (the density θ; Simon 3.14, first paragraph and (1); 2.35).
A1. (Representation.) R is IM, so it has an IMRep (V, θ₀, ξ):
 - V ⊆ ℝ^{n+1} is Borel;
 - θ₀ : ℝ^{n+1} → ℕ is measurable, θ₀ ≥ 1 on V, and ∫_{V∩K}θ₀ dH^{n+1} < ∞ for every compact K;
 - ξ is a.e. strongly measurable for H^{n+1}⌞V;
 - for H^{n+1}-a.e. x ∈ V there is a subspace Q with IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ(x)) Q;
 - R(ω) = ∫_Vθ₀(x)ξ(x)(ω(x)) dH^{n+1}(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^{n+1}(ℝ^{n+1}).
A2. (Hausdorff = Lebesgue.) H^{n+1} = L^{n+1} on ℝ^{n+1} (Mathlib EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume).
A3. (Orientations are ±e_0∧⋯∧e_n.) Let D be the determinant (n+1)-covector of the standard basis, D(v) := det[⟨e_i, v_j⟩]; then D(e) = 1. Every (n+1)-covector α equals α(e)·D (Mathlib AlternatingMap.eq_smul_basis_det, applied to the underlying alternating map). If IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ(x)) Q, there is an orthonormal τ : Fin (n+1) → ℝ^{n+1} with ξ(x)(α) = ±α(τ) for all α. Then τ is an orthonormal basis of ℝ^{n+1}, so D(τ) is the determinant of an orthogonal matrix, i.e. ±1 (Mathlib OrthonormalBasis.det_to_matrix_orthonormalBasis_real). Hence ξ(x)(α) = ±D(τ)α(e) = s(x)·α(e) with s(x) := ξ(x)(D) ∈ {−1, 1}, for H^{n+1}-a.e. x ∈ V.
A4. (The density θ₁; Simon's θ̃.) x ↦ ξ(x)(D) is a.e. strongly measurable for H^{n+1}⌞V (evaluation at D is continuous and linear). So there is a Borel s̃ equal to it H^{n+1}⌞V-a.e. Define
 - θ₁(x) := θ₀(x) if x ∈ V and s̃(x) > 0;
 - θ₁(x) := −θ₀(x) if x ∈ V and s̃(x) ≤ 0;
 - θ₁(x) := 0 if x ∉ V.
 θ₁ is Borel and integer valued with |θ₁| = θ₀1_V. For a.e. x ∈ V, θ₀(x)ξ(x)(ω(x)) = θ₁(x)ω(x)(e). By steps A1–A3, R(ω) = ∫θ₁(x)ω(x)(e) dL^{n+1}(x) for every ω (Simon's (1)), and ∫_K|θ₁| dL^{n+1} = ∫_{V∩K}θ₀ dH^{n+1} < ∞ for compact K.
A5. (θ₁ = 0 a.e. off spt R.) Z := ℝ^{n+1} ∖ spt R is the zero region, which is open (SimonGMT isOpen_zeroRegion; spt R = univ ∖ zeroRegion). Let a ∈ C_c^∞(ℝ^{n+1}) with tsupport a ⊆ Z, and ω_a := a·D. This is a test form with tsupport ω_a ⊆ tsupport a, which is disjoint from spt R. So R(ω_a) = 0 by vanish_off_support. On the other hand R(ω_a) = ∫θ₁a dL^{n+1} by step A4, since ω_a(x)(e) = a(x). θ₁ is locally integrable on Z, so by the fundamental lemma of the calculus of variations (Mathlib IsOpen.ae_eq_zero_of_integral_contDiff_smul_eq_zero), θ₁ = 0 L^{n+1}-a.e. on Z.
A6. (Output.) Put θ := θ₁·1_{spt R}. spt R is closed, hence Borel, so θ is Borel and integer valued, and θ(x) = 0 for x ∉ spt R. |θ| ≤ |θ₁| gives local integrability. θ = θ₁ a.e. by step A5, so R(ω) = ∫θ(x)ω(x)(e) dL^{n+1}(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^{n+1}(ℝ^{n+1}).
Part B (layers and truncation bounds; Simon 3.14 (3)–(7), 3.15).
B1. (Density.) Part A gives a Borel θ : ℝ^{n+1} → ℤ, locally integrable, with θ = 0 off spt R and R(ω) = ∫θω(e) dL for every ω. As spt R is compact, θ is integrable and has compact support.
B2. (Layers.) U_j := {θ ≥ j} (j ∈ ℤ) is Borel with U_{j+1} ⊆ U_j; let V_j := ℝ^{n+1} ∖ U_j. For an integer t, #{j ≥ 1 : t ≥ j} = t⁺ and #{j ≤ 0 : t < j} = t⁻. So Σ_{j≥1}1_{U_j} = θ⁺ and Σ_{j≤0}1_{V_j} = θ⁻ pointwise, and θ = Σ_{j≥1}1_{U_j} − Σ_{j≤0}1_{V_j} (Simon, before (3)).
B3. (Currents X_j = [[U_j]].) X_j(ω) := ∫_{U_j}ω(x)(e) dL is linear in ω. It is sequentially continuous on 𝒟^{n+1}(ℝ^{n+1}): a sequence converging to 0 in 𝒟 has supports in one compact K and converges uniformly, and |X_j(ω)| ≤ L(K)·sup|ω(·)(e)|. So X_j ∈ 𝒟_{n+1}(ℝ^{n+1}).
B4. (Series; Simon (3)–(4).) Fix η ∈ 𝒟^n and let g := dη(·)(e) = div φ_η (S3), continuous with compact support.
 (a) ∂X_j(η) = X_j(dη) = ∫_{U_j}g. For j ≤ 0, ∫_{U_j}g = ∫g − ∫_{V_j}g = −∫_{V_j}g by (S5).
 (b) Hence Σ_j|∂X_j(η)| ≤ Σ_{j≥1}∫1_{U_j}|g| + Σ_{j≤0}∫1_{V_j}|g| = ∫|θ||g| < ∞, by monotone convergence and step B2.
 (c) By dominated convergence for series (Mathlib integral_tsum, with dominating function |θ||g|), the sum is ∫(Σ_{j≥1}1_{U_j} − Σ_{j≤0}1_{V_j})g = ∫θg = R(dη) = ∂R(η). In ℝ, absolute summability gives HasSum. This is (i).
B5. (Variation bound; 3.15/2.35.) Let Λ := M(∂R). If Λ = ∞, (ii) and (iii) are trivial, so assume Λ < ∞.
 (a) Smooth fields. For a C^∞ compactly supported φ with |φ| ≤ 1, ⋆φ is a test form with |⋆φ(x)| ≤ 1 (S2, S4), and ∂R(⋆φ) = R(d⋆φ) = ∫θ div φ (S1, S3). So ∫θ div φ ≤ Λ, and with −φ, |∫θ div φ| ≤ Λ.
 (b) C¹ fields. Let g be C¹ and compactly supported with |g| ≤ 1. The mollifications g_δ := ρ_δ*g (ρ_δ as in step B6) are C^∞, supported in a fixed compact set, satisfy |g_δ| ≤ 1, and div g_δ = ρ_δ*div g → div g uniformly. As θ is integrable, |∫θ div g| = lim_δ|∫θ div g_δ| ≤ Λ.
B6. (Mollification; Ch. 2, 2.5.) Fix ρ ∈ C_c^∞(ℝ^{n+1}) with ρ ≥ 0, ρ(−x) = ρ(x) and ∫ρ = 1, and put ρ_σ(x) := σ^{−(n+1)}ρ(x/σ) (σ > 0). Each ρ_σ is C¹, compactly supported, nonnegative, even and has integral 1. θ_σ := ρ_σ*θ is C^∞ with compact support, and θ_σ → θ in L¹ as σ ↓ 0. By mollify_variation (u := θ, M := Λ, η := ρ_σ; its hypotheses hold by steps B1 and B5), ∫|Dθ_σ| dL ≤ Λ for every σ > 0.
B7. (Smoothed layers; Simon (5)–(6).)
 (a) The function Ψ. Let ε ∈ (0, 1/8] and integers a ≤ b. Choose ψ ∈ C^∞(ℝ), nondecreasing, with ψ = 0 on (−∞, −1 + ε], ψ = 1 on [−ε, ∞) and 0 ≤ ψ' ≤ 1 + 3ε. To build it, integrate a C^∞ function β ≥ 0 supported in [−1 + ε, −ε] with ∫β = 1 and max β ≤ 1 + 3ε; this is possible since the interval has length 1 − 2ε and (1 − 2ε)(1 + 3ε) > 1. Put Ψ(t) := Σ_{j=a}^{b}ψ(t − j).
 (b) Properties. For integer t, ψ(t − j) = 1 if t ≥ j and 0 if t ≤ j − 1, so Ψ∘θ = Σ_{j=a}^{b}1_{U_j}. The supports of ψ'(· − j) lie in the pairwise disjoint intervals [j − 1 + ε, j − ε], so 0 ≤ Ψ' ≤ 1 + 3ε and Ψ is (1 + 3ε)-Lipschitz.
 (c) Integration by parts. Let φ be C^∞ with compact support and |φ| ≤ 1. Since θ_σ has compact support, u_σ := Ψ(θ_σ) − Ψ(0) is C^∞ with compact support. By (S5) and div(u_σφ) = Du_σ(φ) + u_σ div φ, ∫Ψ(θ_σ)div φ = ∫u_σ div φ = −∫Ψ'(θ_σ)Dθ_σ(φ) ≤ (1 + 3ε)∫|Dθ_σ| ≤ (1 + 3ε)Λ.
 (d) Limit. |Ψ(θ_σ) − Ψ(θ)| ≤ (1 + 3ε)|θ_σ − θ| → 0 in L¹, and div φ is bounded. So ∫(Σ_{j=a}^{b}1_{U_j})div φ = ∫Ψ(θ)div φ = lim_σ∫Ψ(θ_σ)div φ ≤ (1 + 3ε)Λ. Letting ε ↓ 0, ∫(Σ_{j=a}^{b}1_{U_j})div φ ≤ Λ.
B8. (Masses; Simon (7).) Let a ≤ b be integers and Y ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^{n+1}) with Y(η) = Σ_{j=a}^{b}∂X_j(η) for all η. Let η be admissible (|η(x)| ≤ 1 for all x). By step B4(a), Y(η) = Σ_{j=a}^{b}∫_{U_j}div φ_η = ∫(Σ_{j=a}^{b}1_{U_j})div φ_η. This is ≤ Λ by step B7, because φ_η is C^∞, compactly supported and |φ_η| = |η| ≤ 1 (S2, S4). Hence M(Y) = sup ofReal(Y(η)) ≤ Λ. Taking a = b = j and Y = ∂X_j gives (ii); taking a = −N, b = N gives (iii). ∎
proof_key_steps: An IMRep (V, θ₀, ξ) of R has ξ(x) = ±(orthonormal basis of ℝ^{n+1}), hence ξ(x)(α) = s(x)α(e₀,…,e_n) with s = ±1, because top-degree covectors are multiples of det.
With H^{n+1} = L^{n+1}, θ₁ := s·θ₀·1_V is Borel, integer valued and locally integrable, and R(ω) = ∫θ₁ω(e).
Off spt R, R kills a·det for a ∈ C_c^∞ (vanish_off_support), so θ = 0 a.e. there and θ := θ₁·1_{spt R} is an integrable integer density with compact support representing R.
U_j := {θ ≥ j} are nested Borel sets and θ = Σ_{j≥1}1_{U_j} − Σ_{j≤0}1_{V_j}.
∂X_j(η) = ∫_{U_j} div φ_η (Hodge correspondence), and Σ_j |∂X_j(η)| ≤ ∫|θ||div φ_η|, so the series converges to ∫θ div φ_η = ∂R(η).
M(∂R) bounds |∫θ div g| for C¹ fields |g| ≤ 1, and mollify_variation gives ∫|D(ρ_σ*θ)| ≤ M(∂R).
Simon's ψ_j smoothing: Ψ = Σ_{j=a}^b ψ(· − j) is (1+3ε)-Lipschitz with Ψ∘θ = Σ_{j=a}^b 1_{U_j}, so ∫(Σ 1_{U_j}) div φ ≤ (1+3ε)M(∂R).
Hence every partial sum Σ_{j=a}^b ∂X_j, and in particular each ∂X_j, has mass ≤ M(∂R).

subproblems.title: De Giorgi's structure theorem for a set of finite perimeter in ℝ^{n+1}: rectifiable reduced boundary, Gauss–Green formula and half-space blow-ups (Simon Ch. 3, 4.1–4.3)
subproblems.statement: Let n ≥ 1, let E ⊆ ℝ^{n+1} be Borel and C ∈ ℝ, and assume ∫_E div φ dL^{n+1} ≤ C for every C^∞ compactly supported φ : ℝ^{n+1} → ℝ^{n+1} with |φ| ≤ 1 everywhere (div φ = trace Dφ, L^{n+1} = volume). Then there are a Borel set B ⊆ ℝ^{n+1} and a Borel map ν : ℝ^{n+1} → ℝ^{n+1} such that: B is countably n-rectifiable and H^n(B) < ∞ (H^n = μHE[n]); |ν(y)| = 1 for y ∈ B; for H^n-a.e. y ∈ B the approximate tangent space of B at y (Simon Ch. 3, 1.4; SimonGMT HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt) is (span{ν(y)})^⊥; ∫_E div φ dL^{n+1} = −∫_B ⟨φ, ν⟩ dH^n for every C¹ compactly supported φ; and for H^n-a.e. y ∈ B and every ρ ∈ ℝ, L^{n+1}((E_{y,r} Δ {w : ⟨w, ν(y)⟩ > 0}) ∩ B_ρ(0)) → 0 as r ↓ 0, where E_{y,r} := {w : y + rw ∈ E}.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 3, 4.1–4.3 (De Giorgi; chapter-03.txt lines 551–746), for U = ℝ^{n+1}. Also used:
- Ch. 2, 2.1–2.2 and 2.5–2.6 (BV functions, mollification, compactness; chapter-02.txt lines 477–626);
- Ch. 1, 3.23 and 4.16 (differentiation of Radon measures; compactness of Radon measures).
This is the De Giorgi input of step 8 of the parent proof. Simon's 3.14 uses 4.3(‡), the half-space blow-up, for the compatibility of the normals of nested sets; the OCR has lost the symbol, and the supplied text writes '4.3(∗)' for the same item.
Errata applied:
- (i) The OCR of 4.1 drops the minus sign. For the inward normal ν the identity is ∫_E div g dL^{n+1} = −∫⟨g, ν⟩ dμ_E.
- (ii) The limit set (9) is {z^{n+1} > c}, not '<': with inward normal e_{n+1}, the blow-ups converge to the upper half-space, consistent with (‡).
- (iii) The printed first sentence of the proof of 4.3 ('By 1.6 and 3.6 of Ch. 1 the first part follows from (†)') is a whole argument: comparison of μ with H^n, the rectifiability criterion of Ch. 3, 1.6 '⇐' for a measure with flat tangent measures, density one of rectifiable sets, and Radon–Nikodym. Here it is supplied in step 5 by the accepted siblings measure_eq_hausdorff and rect_density_one, whose hypotheses are verified there. Those siblings produce rectifiability and the identity μ = H^n⌞B together, from the tangent-measure convergence of step 4(f) alone. So no step uses μ = H^n⌞B before it is established.
Siblings used: gauss_green_measure (codim1_rdo_dg_gauss_green_measure), the Riesz-representation step 4.1; measure_eq_hausdorff (codim1_rdo_dg_measure_eq_hausdorff); rect_density_one (codim1_rdo_rectifiable_ae_density_one).
Notation: L := L^{n+1} = volume = μHE[n+1]; H^n := μHE[n]; ω_k := L^k(B_1); div φ := trace Dφ; η_{y,λ}(z) := λ^{−1}(z − y); E_{y,λ} := η_{y,λ}(E) = {w : y + λw ∈ E}; C₊ := max(C, 0).
1. (Gauss–Green measure; 4.1.) The hypothesis holds with C_K := C for every compact K. So gauss_green_measure (m := n, D := ℝ^{n+1}, F := E) gives a Borel measure μ with μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K, and a Borel ν with |ν(y)| = 1 for every y, such that (4.1) ∫_E div φ dL = −∫⟨φ, ν⟩ dμ for every C¹ compactly supported φ.
2. (Finite total mass.)
 (a) Continuous test fields. Let g be C¹ and compactly supported with |g| ≤ 1. Its mollifications g_ε are C^∞, have |g_ε| ≤ 1, supports in a fixed compact set, and div g_ε → div g uniformly. The hypothesis for −g_ε gives −∫_E div g_ε ≤ C, so ∫⟨g, ν⟩dμ = −∫_E div g ≤ C₊. By uniform approximation, ∫⟨g, ν⟩ dμ ≤ C₊ for every continuous compactly supported g with |g| ≤ 1.
 (b) μ(K) ≤ C₊. Let K be compact and κ > 0. By Lusin there is a compact K' ⊆ K with μ(K ∖ K') < κ and ν|_{K'} continuous. Choose an open W ⊇ K with μ(W ∖ K) < κ. Extend ν|_{K'} to a continuous unit-bounded g (Tietze, then radial retraction onto the unit ball), and multiply it by χ ∈ C_c(W; [0, 1]) with χ = 1 on K'. Then ∫⟨χg, ν⟩dμ ≥ μ(K') − μ(W ∖ K') ≥ μ(K) − 3κ. So μ(K) ≤ C₊ for every compact K, and μ(ℝ^{n+1}) ≤ C₊.
3. (Reduced boundary; 4.2.) Let ∂*E be the set of y ∈ spt μ at which ν_E(y) := lim_{ρ↓0}μ(B̄_ρ(y))^{−1}∫_{B̄_ρ(y)}ν dμ exists and |ν_E(y)| = 1. By differentiation of Radon measures (Ch. 1, 3.23; Mathlib VitaliFamily.ae_tendsto_average with the Besicovitch family), these averages tend to ν(y) for μ-a.e. y. Hence μ(ℝ^{n+1} ∖ ∂*E) = 0 and ν_E = ν μ-a.e.
4. (Blow-up at y ∈ ∂*E; printed proof of 4.3, (1)–(12).) After a rigid motion, y = 0 and ν_E(0) = e_{n+1}. Put E_λ := E_{0,λ}, μ_λ(A) := λ^{−n}μ(λA) and ν_λ(z) := ν(λz); then (4.1) holds for (E_λ, μ_λ, ν_λ).
 (a) (1)–(2): ⨍_{B_ρ}ν^{n+1}dμ → 1 and ⨍_{B_ρ}|ν^i|dμ → 0 for i ≤ n, as ρ ↓ 0.
 (b) (3)–(6): test (4.1) with g = ζ_ke_{n+1}, where ζ_k are Lipschitz radial cut-offs decreasing to 1_{B̄_ρ}. This gives ∫_{B̄_ρ}ν^{n+1}dμ ≤ (d/dρ)L(E ∩ B_ρ) ≤ H^n(∂B_ρ) for a.e. small ρ. With (1), μ(B_ρ) ≤ 2(d/dρ)L(E ∩ B_ρ) ≤ 2(n+1)ω_{n+1}ρ^n for ρ < ρ₁, so μ_λ(B_R) ≤ cR^n.
 (c) (7): by the BV compactness theorem (Ch. 2, 2.6), along any λ_k ↓ 0 a subsequence has 1_{E_{λ_k}} → 1_F in L¹_loc, with F of locally finite perimeter.
 (d) (8)–(9): for ζ ∈ C_c^1 and i ≤ n, |∫_{E_λ}D_iζ| ≤ sup|ζ|·λ^{−n}∫_{B_{λR}}|ν^i|dμ → 0, so F = ℝ^n × H. For ζ ≥ 0, (4.1) and (1) give ∫_FD_{n+1}ζ = lim(−∫ζν_λ^{n+1}dμ_λ) ≤ 0. So 1_H is nondecreasing and F = {z^{n+1} > c} (erratum ii).
 (e) (10)–(11): apply the Sobolev inequality for BV functions (by mollification, Ch. 2, 2.5; Mathlib lintegral_pow_le_pow_lintegral_fderiv) to ζ1_E, using D(ζ1_E) = ζD1_E + 1_EDζ and (6). It gives V^{n/(n+1)} ≤ c·(d/dρ)V for V(ρ) := L(E ∩ B_ρ), which is positive because 0 ∈ spt μ. Integrating, L(E ∩ B_ρ) ≥ c'ρ^{n+1} for small ρ, and the same holds for the complement (normal −ν). These scale-invariant bounds pass to F and force c = 0. The limit is unique, so 1_{E_λ} → 1_{{z^{n+1} > 0}} in L¹_loc as λ ↓ 0. This is (‡).
 (f) (12): put P₀ := {z^{n+1} = 0} = ν_E(0)^⊥.
  - By (4.1) and L¹_loc convergence, ν_λμ_λ → e_{n+1}H^n⌞P₀ weakly.
  - Weak subsequential limits μ* of μ_λ exist by (6) and Ch. 1, 4.16, and H^n⌞P₀ ≤ μ*, since the variation of a weak limit is at most the limit of the variations.
  - Testing with ζe_{n+1}, 1_{B_R} ≤ ζ ≤ 1_{B_{R+ε}}, and using (1): ∫(1 − ν_λ^{n+1})dμ_λ → 0 on B_{R+ε}. So μ*(B_R) ≤ ω_nR^n = H^n⌞P₀(B_R).
  - Hence every subsequential limit is μ* = H^n⌞P₀ (4.3(†)). Every sequence λ_k ↓ 0 has a subsequence along which μ_{λ_k} converges, and all such limits agree. So ∫f dμ_λ → ∫_{P₀}f dH^n as λ ↓ 0, for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^{n+1}).
5. (Rectifiable carrier and μ = H^n⌞B; the first sentence of the proof of 4.3.) Let G := {y ∈ ∂*E : ν_E(y) = ν(y)}; μ(ℝ^{n+1} ∖ G) = 0 by step 3.
 (a) Flat tangent measures. Let y ∈ G and f ∈ C_c(ℝ^{n+1}). Undo the rigid motion of step 4: Φ(z) := Q(z − y) with Q orthogonal and Qν(y) = e_{n+1}. Then ∫f dμ_λ in step 4 is λ^{−n}∫(f∘Q)(λ^{−1}(z − y))dμ(z). Also Q^{−1}P₀ = (span{ν(y)})^⊥, and H^n is invariant under orthogonal maps. So step 4(f), applied to f∘Q^{−1}, gives
  (FT) r^{−n}∫f(r^{−1}(z − y))dμ(z) → ∫_{(span{ν(y)})^⊥} f dH^n as r ↓ 0,
  for every y ∈ G, hence for μ-a.e. y, and for every continuous compactly supported f.
 (b) Apply measure_eq_hausdorff with m := n ≥ 1, D := ℝ^{n+1} (open), and μ, ν from step 1. Its hypotheses:
  - μ(ℝ^{n+1} ∖ D) = μ(∅) = 0, and μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K (step 1);
  - ν is Borel with |ν(y)| = 1 for every y (step 1);
  - (FT) holds for μ-a.e. y and every continuous compactly supported f (step 5(a));
  - (RD): for every Borel countably n-rectifiable S ⊆ ℝ^{n+1} with H^n(S) < ∞, H^n(S ∩ B_t(w))/(ω_nt^n) → 1 as t ↓ 0 for H^n-a.e. w ∈ S. This is exactly rect_density_one with P := n + 1 and n := n (n ≥ 1).
  It gives a Borel, countably n-rectifiable B ⊆ ℝ^{n+1} with μ = H^n⌞B as measures. For H^n-a.e. y ∈ B, the approximate tangent space of B at y (Simon Ch. 3, 1.4) is (span{ν(y)})^⊥.
6. (Output.)
 - B is Borel and countably n-rectifiable, and H^n(B) = μ(ℝ^{n+1}) ≤ C₊ < ∞ by step 2(b).
 - ν is Borel and |ν(y)| = 1 for every y, in particular on B.
 - For H^n-a.e. y ∈ B, B has approximate tangent space (span{ν(y)})^⊥ at y (step 5).
 - Gauss–Green: by (4.1) and μ = H^n⌞B, ∫_E div φ dL = −∫⟨φ, ν⟩dμ = −∫_B⟨φ, ν⟩dH^n for every C¹ compactly supported φ.
 - (‡): choose a Borel N ⊇ ℝ^{n+1} ∖ G with μ(N) = 0. Then H^n(B ∩ N) = μ(N) = 0. Let y ∈ B ∖ N, so y ∈ G and ν_E(y) = ν(y). Step 4(e), transported back by the rigid motion (L is invariant under orthogonal maps, and B_ρ(0) is rotation invariant), gives L((E_{y,r} Δ {w : ⟨w, ν(y)⟩ > 0}) ∩ B_ρ(0)) → 0 as r ↓ 0, for every ρ ∈ ℝ (B_ρ(0) = ∅ if ρ ≤ 0). So this holds for H^n⌞B-a.e. y. ∎
proof_key_steps: gauss_green_measure gives μ and a unit Borel ν with ∫_E div φ = −∫⟨φ, ν⟩dμ; the perimeter bound gives μ(ℝ^{n+1}) ≤ max(C, 0).
Besicovitch differentiation: μ is carried by the reduced boundary ∂*E, where the normal averages converge to ν.
Blow-up at y ∈ ∂*E (printed 4.3 (1)–(12)): E_{y,λ} tends in L¹_loc to the half-space {⟨w, ν⟩ > 0} (‡), and λ^{−n}μ(y + λ·) → H^n⌞ν(y)^⊥ for the whole family λ ↓ 0.

measure_eq_hausdorff, with (RD) supplied by rect_density_one at P := n + 1, turns these flat tangent measures into a Borel countably n-rectifiable B with μ = H^n⌞B and approximate tangent planes ν^⊥ a.e.; no step uses μ = H^n⌞B before it is obtained.
Output: H^n(B) = μ(ℝ^{n+1}) < ∞, the Gauss–Green formula over B, and (‡) at H^n⌞B-a.e. point.

subproblems.title: A sum of boundaries of nested sets of finite perimeter with bounded partial masses is integer multiplicity (Simon 6.3.14 (8)–(9), 3.15, Ch. 3, 4.3(‡))
subproblems.statement: Let n ≥ 1, let U_j ⊆ ℝ^{n+1} (j ∈ ℤ) be Borel sets with U_{j+1} ⊆ U_j, and let X_j ∈ 𝒟_{n+1}(ℝ^{n+1}) with X_j(ω) = ∫_{U_j} ω(x)(e_0, …, e_n) dL^{n+1}(x) for every ω and M(∂X_j) < ∞ for every j. Let T ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^{n+1}) satisfy HasSum (j ↦ ∂X_j(η)) (T(η)) for every η ∈ 𝒟^n(ℝ^{n+1}), and let C ∈ [0, ∞) be such that M(Y) ≤ C for every N ∈ ℕ and every Y ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^{n+1}) with Y(η) = Σ_{j=−N}^{N} ∂X_j(η) for all η. Then T is integer multiplicity.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (U : ℤ → Set (Euclid (n + 1))) (X : ℤ → GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid (n + 1))) (n + 1)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid (n + 1))) n) (C : ℝ≥0∞), 1 ≤ n → (∀ j, MeasurableSet (U j)) → (∀ j, U (j + 1) ⊆ U j) → (∀ (j : ℤ) (ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid (n + 1))) (n + 1)), X j ω = ∫ x in U j, (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid (n + 1)) (n + 1)) x (fun i => EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ))) → (∀ j, (X j).boundary.mass < ∞) → (∀ η : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid (n + 1))) n, HasSum (fun j => (X j).boundary η) (T η)) → C < ∞ → (∀ (N : ℕ) (Y : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid (n + 1))) n), (∀ η : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid (n + 1))) n, Y η = ∑ j ∈ Finset.Icc (-(N : ℤ)) N, (X j).boundary η) → Y.mass ≤ C) → IsIntegerMultiplicity T
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, proof of 3.14, (8)–(9) and its final paragraph (chapter-06.txt lines 1105–1132). Also Remark 3.15 (∂[[A]] = τ(∂*A, 1, ⋆ν_A); lines 1000–1029) and Ch. 3, 4.3(‡) for the normals of nested sets: 'By virtue of the fact that U_{j+1} ⊂ U_j we see from 4.3(‡) of Ch. 3 that ν_j ≡ ν_k on ∂*U_j ∩ ∂*U_k'. These are steps 8–9 of the parent proof.
Siblings used: de_giorgi; normal_orientation (codim1_lur_normal_covector_orientation); im_calculus (cmc_imRep_locality_restrict_sub, parts (a) and (d)); oriented_mass_lower (codim1_oriented_rep_lintegral_le_massOn).
Notation:
- The Hodge correspondence (S1)–(S5) is as in the sibling layers: α_î := α(e_{i.succAbove 0}, …, e_{i.succAbove(n−1)}), (⋆φ)(x)(v) := det[φ(x), v], φ_η^i := (−1)^iη(·)_î, (⋆φ)_î = (−1)^iφ^i, |⋆φ| = |φ|, dη(·)(e) = div φ_η, and ∫div φ = 0.
- For an n-covector α let φ_α := Σ_i(−1)^iα_îe_i, so that φ_η(x) = φ_{η(x)}.
- For v ∈ ℝ^{n+1} let ξ_v be the n-vector ξ_v(α) := −⟨φ_α, v⟩ = −Σ_i(−1)^iα_î⟨e_i, v⟩. It is continuous and linear in α, and linear in v.
- L = volume, H^n = μHE[n], ‖η‖ := sup_x|η(x)|.
1. (Finite perimeter.) Fix j. For a C^∞ compactly supported φ with |φ| ≤ 1, ⋆φ is a test form with |⋆φ(x)| ≤ 1. So ∂X_j(⋆φ) ≤ M(∂X_j) =: C_j < ∞, and ∂X_j(⋆φ) = X_j(d⋆φ) = ∫_{U_j}div φ dL by (S1), (S3). Hence ∫_{U_j}div φ ≤ C_j.
2. (De Giorgi.) de_giorgi (n ≥ 1, E := U_j Borel, C := C_j) gives B_j and ν_j:
 - B_j is Borel and countably n-rectifiable with H^n(B_j) < ∞;
 - ν_j is Borel with |ν_j| = 1 on B_j;
 - B_j has approximate tangent space (span{ν_j(y)})^⊥ at H^n-a.e. y ∈ B_j;
 - ∫_{U_j}div φ = −∫_{B_j}⟨φ, ν_j⟩dH^n for C¹ compactly supported φ;
 - (‡): for H^n-a.e. y ∈ B_j and every ρ, L(((U_j)_{y,r} Δ {⟨w, ν_j(y)⟩ > 0}) ∩ B_ρ(0)) → 0 as r ↓ 0.
3. (∂X_j as a rectifiable current; 3.15.) For η ∈ 𝒟^n, ∂X_j(η) = X_j(dη) = ∫_{U_j}div φ_η = −∫_{B_j}⟨φ_η, ν_j⟩dH^n = ∫_{B_j}ξ_{ν_j(x)}(η(x)) dH^n(x). For |v| = 1, normal_orientation gives an orthonormal family σ_v with span (span{v})^⊥ and α(σ_v) = −⟨φ_α, v⟩ = ξ_v(α) for every α. So IsUnitOrientationOf ξ_v (span{v})^⊥, with the + sign.
4. (Compatibility of normals; 3.14 with 4.3(‡).) Let j < k, so U_k ⊆ U_j. Let y ∈ B_j ∩ B_k be a point where (‡) holds for both (U_j, ν_j) and (U_k, ν_k); H^n-a.e. point of B_j ∩ B_k is such. Put H_i := {w : ⟨w, ν_i(y)⟩ > 0} for i ∈ {j, k}.
 (a) Since (U_k)_{y,r} ⊆ (U_j)_{y,r}, L((H_k ∖ H_j) ∩ B_1) ≤ L((H_k Δ (U_k)_{y,r}) ∩ B_1) + L(((U_j)_{y,r} Δ H_j) ∩ B_1) → 0. So L((H_k ∖ H_j) ∩ B_1) = 0.
 (b) Suppose ν_k(y) ≠ ν_j(y). Then w₀ := (ν_k(y) − ν_j(y))/4 satisfies ⟨w₀, ν_k(y)⟩ > 0 > ⟨w₀, ν_j(y)⟩ and |w₀| ≤ 1/2. So a small ball around w₀ lies in (H_k ∖ H_j) ∩ B_1, contradicting (a).
 Hence ν_j = ν_k H^n-a.e. on B_j ∩ B_k.
5. (Common normal and orientation.) Fix a bijection κ : ℕ → ℤ and let B := ⋃_jB_j (Borel).
 (a) For x ∈ B let i(x) := min{i : x ∈ B_{κ(i)}} and ν(x) := ν_{κ(i(x))}(x); for x ∉ B let ν(x) := e_0. Then ν is Borel and |ν| = 1 on B.
 (b) By step 4 (countably many pairs), ν = ν_j H^n-a.e. on B_j for every j.
 (c) Put ξ(x) := ξ_{ν(x)}, a Borel map. By step 3, ∂X_j(η) = ∫_{B_j}ξ(x)(η(x)) dH^n(x) for all j and η, and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ(x)) (span{ν(x)})^⊥ for every x ∈ B.
6. (Mass bound; Simon (7)–(8).) Fix N ∈ ℕ, J := {−N, …, N}, h_N := Σ_{j∈J}1_{B_j} and M_N := ⋃_{j∈J}B_j.
 (a) Y_N(η) := Σ_{j∈J}∂X_j(η) is a current (a finite sum of currents), so M(Y_N) ≤ C by hypothesis. By step 5, Y_N(η) = ∫_{M_N}h_N(x)ξ(x)(η(x)) dH^n(x).
 (b) Apply oriented_mass_lower with U = V = W := ℝ^{n+1}, M' := M_N, θ' := h_N (Borel, ≥ 0) and ξ' := ξ (Borel, a unit orientation at every point of M_N). Since I := ∫_{M_N}h_N dH^n = Σ_{j∈J}H^n(B_j) < ∞, it gives I ≤ M(Y_N) ≤ C.
 (c) Letting N → ∞, Σ_{j∈ℤ}H^n(B_j) ≤ C < ∞.
7. (Multiplicity.) h := Σ_{j∈ℤ}1_{B_j} : ℝ^{n+1} → [0, ∞] is Borel with ∫h dH^n = Σ_jH^n(B_j) ≤ C, so h < ∞ H^n-a.e. Let M := {x ∈ B : h(x) < ∞}, a Borel set with H^n(B ∖ M) = 0. Put θ(x) := h(x) ∈ ℕ for x ∈ M and θ(x) := 0 otherwise. Then θ is Borel, θ ≥ 1 on M, and ∫_{M∩K}θ dH^n ≤ C for every K.
8. (Rectifiability and tangent planes.)
 (a) M ⊆ ⋃_jB_j is countably n-rectifiable: use countable unions (SimonGMT countablyRectifiable_iUnion, indexed via κ) and subsets. Also H^n(M) ≤ Σ_jH^n(B_j) < ∞.
 (b) For each j, apply im_calculus (a) with U = ℝ^{n+1} to the Borel pairs B_j ∩ M ⊆ M and B_j ∩ M ⊆ B_j; the larger sets have finite H^n-measure. For H^n-a.e. x ∈ B_j ∩ M and every subspace Q: M has approximate tangent space Q at x ⟺ B_j ∩ M does ⟺ B_j does.
 (c) By step 2 and ν = ν_j a.e. on B_j, for H^n-a.e. x ∈ B_j ∩ M, M has approximate tangent space (span{ν(x)})^⊥ at x, and ξ(x) is a unit orientation of it (step 5). As M = ⋃_j(B_j ∩ M), this holds for H^n-a.e. x ∈ M.
9. (IMRep.) By steps 7–8, (M, θ, ξ) is an IMRep in ℝ^{n+1} of degree n:
 - M is Borel, contained in ℝ^{n+1}, and countably n-rectifiable;
 - θ is measurable, positive on M and locally integrable;
 - ξ is Borel, hence a.e. strongly measurable;
 - for H^n-a.e. x ∈ M, Q := (span{ν(x)})^⊥ satisfies HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ x) Q.
 By im_calculus (d), |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for H^n-a.e. x ∈ M and every α.
10. (It represents T.) Fix η ∈ 𝒟^n. By hypothesis T(η) = Σ_{j∈ℤ}∂X_j(η) (HasSum), and ∂X_j(η) = ∫1_{B_j}ξ(η)dH^n by step 5.
 (a) Domination. H^n(B_j ∖ M) = 0 and |ξ(x)(η(x))| ≤ ‖η‖ for a.e. x ∈ M (step 9). So Σ_j∫|1_{B_j}ξ(η)|dH^n ≤ ‖η‖Σ_jH^n(B_j) < ∞.
 (b) By dominated convergence for series (Mathlib integral_tsum), Σ_j∫_{B_j}ξ(η)dH^n = ∫hξ(η)dH^n = ∫_Mθξ(η)dH^n, because h = θ on M, H^n(B ∖ M) = 0 and h = 0 off B.
 (c) By uniqueness of sums, T(η) = ∫_Mθ(x)ξ(x)(η(x)) dH^n(x) = (M, θ, ξ).action(η).
 Hence T is integer multiplicity. ∎
proof_key_steps: M(∂X_j) < ∞ means U_j has finite perimeter (Hodge correspondence), so de_giorgi gives B_j, ν_j with Gauss–Green, tangent planes ν_j^⊥ and half-space blow-ups.
∂X_j(η) = ∫_{B_j} ξ_{ν_j}(η) dH^n with ξ_ν(α) = −⟨φ_α, ν⟩, which normal_orientation identifies as a unit orientation of ν^⊥ (Simon 3.15).
Nested sets have nested half-space blow-ups, so ν_j = ν_k a.e. on B_j ∩ B_k; one Borel normal ν and orientation ξ serve all j.
oriented_mass_lower gives Σ_{|j|≤N} H^n(B_j) ≤ M(Σ_{|j|≤N} ∂X_j) ≤ C, so h := Σ_j 1_{B_j} is integrable.
(⋃B_j ∩ {h<∞}, h, ξ) is an IMRep (rectifiable union; tangent planes by im_calculus (a)), and dominated convergence for the series shows it represents T.

subproblems.title: Support lemma (Simon 6.2.11): a current vanishes on test forms supported away from its support (reused accepted dtc_vanish_off_support)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P any set, S ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U n) and ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) (TestFormOn U n) with tsupport ω disjoint from spt S, where spt S = U ∖ Z_S and Z_S is the union of all open W with closure W compact, closure W ⊆ U and S(η) = 0 for every η ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport η ⊆ W (GeometricCurrentOn.support). Then S(ω) = 0.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (S : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (ω : TestFormOn U n), Disjoint (tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n)) S.support → S ω = 0
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reuse. This child is the comparator-accepted declaration dtc_vanish_off_support (DAG node root.density_and_tangent_cones-a1.vanish_off_support-a1, status accepted, accepted candidate commit 44ef61f79e2168134f8a5a6d6520baba56052d67). It is reused with its identical frozen type: a whitespace-normalised comparison with the declaration in that commit matches. That commit's GMT/Ch07/Contract.lean is byte-identical to the frozen contract, its only sorry is the frozen root theorem, and it declares no axioms. Role here: It is used by layers (step A5) to show that R vanishes on the test forms a·det supported in ℝ^{n+1} ∖ spt R, so that the density θ can be chosen to vanish off spt R. The proof below is the accepted proof of this declaration, copied verbatim.

Source: Simon Ch. 6, 2.11 (definition of spt T, chapter-06.txt lines 297–301); the partition-of-unity argument below is the standard reason why the union in 2.11 is itself a set on which the current vanishes. Notation: "S vanishes on W" means S(η) = 0 for every η ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport η ⊆ W.
1. K := tsupport ω is compact and K ⊆ U, because ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) is a compactly supported smooth form with tsupport ω ⊆ U. If K = ∅ then ω = 0 and S(ω) = 0 by linearity; assume K ≠ ∅.
2. Since K ⊆ U and K ∩ spt S = ∅, we have K ⊆ U ∖ spt S ⊆ Z_S. By compactness there are finitely many open sets W₁,…,W_m from the family defining Z_S (each with S vanishing on W_i) such that K ⊆ W₁ ∪ … ∪ W_m.
3. Take a smooth partition of unity on ℝ^P subordinate to the open cover {W₁,…,W_m, ℝ^P ∖ K} (e.g. Mathlib's SmoothPartitionOfUnity.exists_isSubordinate for the closed set K and the cover by W₁,…,W_m): smooth ψ₁,…,ψ_m : ℝ^P → [0,1] with tsupport ψ_i ⊆ W_i for each i and Σ_i ψ_i(y) = 1 for every y ∈ K.
4. For each i, ψ_iω (pointwise product of a smooth function and a smooth n-form) is smooth, and tsupport(ψ_iω) ⊆ tsupport ψ_i ∩ tsupport ω ⊆ W_i ∩ K; in particular it is compact and contained in U. Thus ψ_iω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport(ψ_iω) ⊆ W_i, and S(ψ_iω) = 0 since S vanishes on W_i.
5. ω = Σ_i ψ_iω pointwise: if ω(y) ≠ 0 then y ∈ K and Σ_iψ_i(y) = 1; if ω(y) = 0 both sides vanish. By linearity of S, S(ω) = Σ_i S(ψ_iω) = 0.

subproblems.title: Basic calculus of integer multiplicity representations: locality of approximate tangent spaces, restriction, differences, orientation bound (reused accepted cmc_imRep_locality_restrict_sub)

(b) If U ⊆ ℝ^P is open, R = (M, θ, ξ) is an IMRep in U (contract structure) and E is Borel, then (M ∩ E, θ, ξ) is an IMRep in U and it represents some current in 𝒟_n(U). (c) If U is open and A, B ∈ 𝒟_n(U) are integer multiplicity (contract IsIntegerMultiplicity), then so is A − B. (d) For every IMRep R in any U, for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ R.carrier, |R.orient(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for every n-covector α (|·| the Euclidean coefficient norm).

Source: Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.5(2) and the density argument in the proof of Theorem 1.6 “⇒” (chapter-03.txt lines 107–160); Ch. 6, Remarks 3.2(1) and 2.9 (chapter-06.txt lines 287–293, 755–768), stated in the book without proof; and Ch. 6, Remark 2.6 for the orientation bound. Hⁿ := μHE[n] throughout. For x ∈ ℝ^P and r > 0, η_{x,r}(y) := r⁻¹(y − x) (SimonGMT blowUpMap). The statement has four parts: (a) locality of approximate tangent spaces, (b) restriction of a representation to a Borel set, (c) differences of integer multiplicity currents, (d) the orientation bound |⟨α, ξ⟩| ≤ |α|; U is open in (a)–(c).

Preliminaries.
(P0) Normalization: SimonGMT's density theorems are stated for simonHausdorffOuterMeasureReal n, which equals μHE[n] for natural n (SimonGMT Chapter02 simonHausdorffMeasureReal_nat_eq_euclideanHausdorffMeasure, with simonHausdorffMeasureReal_toOuterMeasure); hence null sets, finiteness and densities transfer verbatim, and Hⁿ is Borel regular (every set has a Borel hull of the same measure).
(P1) Scaling: for every set A, Hⁿ(η_{x,r}(A)) = r^{−n}Hⁿ(A) (Mathlib Measure.hausdorffMeasure_smul₀ and invariance of Hausdorff measure under isometries). Hence for Borel A and bounded Borel f, ∫_{η_{x,r}(A)} f dHⁿ = r^{−n}∫_A f(η_{x,r}(y)) dHⁿ(y).
(P2) Density zero (SimonGMT Chapter01 simon_theorem_3_6, for the Borel regular outer measure Hⁿ, cf. simon_remark_3_7_hausdorff): if D is Borel with Hⁿ(D) < ∞, then for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∉ D, lim_{r↓0} Hⁿ(D ∩ B̄_r(x))/(ω_n rⁿ) = 0.
(P3) Cauchy–Binet. For n×P matrices A, B, det(ABᵀ) = Σ_I det(A_I) det(B_I), the sum over increasing I = (i_1 < ⋯ < i_n) in {1, …, P}, A_I the n×n submatrix of columns I. Proof: the j-th column of ABᵀ is Σ_k B_{jk}A_{·k}, so by multilinearity det(ABᵀ) = Σ_{k_1,…,k_n} B_{1k_1}⋯B_{nk_n} det(A_{·k_1}, …, A_{·k_n}); terms with a repeated index vanish, and grouping the remaining tuples by their underlying increasing tuple I (k = I ∘ σ for a permutation σ) gives Σ_I det(A_I) Σ_σ sgn(σ) Π_j B_{j, I_{σ(j)}} = Σ_I det(A_I)det(B_I). (For n > P both sides are 0 — no increasing I, and rank ABᵀ < n.)
(P4) Orientation bound. If τ_1, …, τ_n are orthonormal in ℝ^P and ⟨α, ζ⟩ = ±α(τ_1, …, τ_n) for all n-covectors α, then |⟨α, ζ⟩| ≤ |α| (Euclidean coefficient norm covectorEuclideanNorm). Proof: with A_{ik} := ⟨τ_i, e_k⟩, multilinearity and the alternating property give α(τ) = Σ_I det(A_I) α(e_I); by Cauchy–Schwarz and (P3), |α(τ)| ≤ |α|(Σ_I det(A_I)²)^{1/2} = |α| det(AAᵀ)^{1/2} = |α|, since AAᵀ = (⟨τ_i, τ_j⟩) is the identity. For n = 0, |α(∅)| = |α|.
(P5) Two unit orientations of the same n-dimensional subspace Q differ by a sign: if τ, τ' are orthonormal bases of Q, τ'_i = Σ_j O_{ij}τ_j with O orthogonal, and α(τ') = det(O)α(τ) = ±α(τ) for every alternating α. Hence IsUnitOrientationOf ζ Q and IsUnitOrientationOf ζ' Q imply ζ' = ζ or ζ' = −ζ, and IsUnitOrientationOf (−ζ) Q holds whenever IsUnitOrientationOf ζ Q.
(P6) If R = (M, θ, ξ) is an IMRep in an open U, then Hⁿ(M ∩ K) ≤ ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U (θ ≥ 1 on M).

(d) Orientation bound. By the orientation field of an IMRep, for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ R.carrier there is Q with IsUnitOrientationOf (R.orient x) Q, i.e. an orthonormal τ with ⟨α, R.orient x⟩ = ±α(τ) for all α; by (P4), |R.orient x α| ≤ |α| for all α. (No openness of U is needed.)

(a) Locality. Let U be open, M ⊆ M' ⊆ U Borel with Hⁿ(M' ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U, and D := M' ∖ M.
1. For R ∈ ℕ let U_R := {x ∈ U : |x| < R, infDist(x, ℝ^P ∖ U) > 1/R} (U_R := {|x| < R} if U = ℝ^P). U_R is open, closure(U_R) is a compact subset of U, and U_R ↑ U. D_R := D ∩ U_R is Borel with Hⁿ(D_R) ≤ Hⁿ(M' ∩ closure(U_R)) < ∞. By (P2) there is an Hⁿ-null set Z_R such that every x ∉ D_R ∪ Z_R satisfies Hⁿ(D_R ∩ B̄_r(x)) = o(rⁿ) as r ↓ 0. Let Z := ⋃_R Z_R, and let Z' ⊇ Z be a Borel Hⁿ-null set (P0). Let x ∈ M ∖ Z'; choose R with x ∈ U_R and r₀ > 0 with B̄_{r₀}(x) ⊆ U_R. Then x ∉ D_R (as x ∈ M) and D ∩ B̄_r(x) = D_R ∩ B̄_r(x) for r < r₀, so Hⁿ(D ∩ B̄_r(x)) = o(rⁿ).
2. Fix such x, a subspace Q and f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P) with spt f ⊆ B_ρ(0). For r < r₀/ρ the sets η_{x,r}(M), η_{x,r}(M') meet B_ρ(0) in sets of finite Hⁿ-measure, so the integrals below are genuine Bochner integrals. Since η_{x,r} is injective, η_{x,r}(M') is the disjoint union of η_{x,r}(M) and η_{x,r}(D), and by (P1)
 |∫_{η_{x,r}(M')} f dHⁿ − ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} f dHⁿ| = |∫_{η_{x,r}(D)} f dHⁿ| ≤ |f|_∞ r^{−n} Hⁿ(D ∩ B_{rρ}(x)) → 0 as r ↓ 0.
Hence for every f the two families of integrals have the same limit as r → 0⁺ or both have none; the condition finrank Q = n is common to both predicates. So HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q ↔ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M' x Q for every x ∈ M ∖ Z' and every Q; the exceptional set M ∩ Z' is null for Hⁿ⌞M. ∎

(b) Restriction. Let R = (M, θ, ξ) be an IMRep in the open set U and E a Borel set. Define R' with carrier M ∩ E and the same mult θ and orient ξ.
1. Structure fields: M ∩ E is Borel and contained in U; countably n-rectifiable (CountablyRectifiable.mono); θ is measurable and θ > 0 on M ∩ E; ∫_{M∩E∩K} θ dHⁿ ≤ ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U; ξ is a.e. strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ E) ≤ Hⁿ⌞M.
2. Orientation: by (P6) and (a) applied to M ∩ E ⊆ M ⊆ U, for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M ∩ E and all Q, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n (M ∩ E) x Q ↔ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q. With the orientation field of R (Hⁿ-a.e. on M) this gives the orientation field of R'.
3. The current: A(ω) := ∫_{M∩E} θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dHⁿ for ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). By (d), |θ⟨ω, ξ⟩| ≤ |ω|_∞ θ 1_{tsupport ω} Hⁿ-a.e. on M, and tsupport ω is a compact subset of U, so the integrand is integrable; A is linear. If ω_j → 0 in 𝒟ⁿ(U) (TestFormOnConverges: supports in a fixed compact K ⊆ U and uniform convergence of all derivatives, in particular |ω_j|_∞ → 0 since all norms on the finite-dimensional space of n-covectors are equivalent), then |A(ω_j)| ≤ |ω_j|_∞ ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ → 0. Source. Simon Ch. 6, 2.5 (the mass M_W(T), chapter-06.txt lines 224–240) and 3.2(3) (M_W(T) = ∫_{M∩W} θ dH^n, chapter-06.txt lines 755–770). This is the lower half of the parent proof: its step 1 and step 3. Steps (3a)–(3b) of the parent (the measure ν = θ'·H^k⌞M', finite on W, and Lusin's theorem) are carried out with the accepted lemma lusin_covector. Steps (3c)–(3e) (Tietze extension, normalization to |·| ≤ 1, mollification, smooth cut-off) are exactly what the accepted lemma smooth_unit_approximation packages: for each δ > 0 it gives one admissible form that is δ-close to L∘ξ' on the Lusin set K. Because that form is δ-close on K, rather than a member of a pointwise convergent sequence, the parent's dominated-convergence passage (3f) is not needed. The parent's estimate (3g) is applied directly to T(ω), with the one extra error term δ·ν(K) (step 8). Measurability of M' (a hypothesis of the parent) is not needed and not assumed: every restriction below is to one of the Borel sets W, Z, A, K, and (H^k⌞M')⌞B = H^k⌞(B ∩ M') for Borel B and an arbitrary set M'.

Sibling children used (accepted declarations, reused with their identical frozen types):
- unit_orientation_dual (Submission.dor_ims_unitOrientation_dual): there is a continuous linear map L : Λ_k(ℝ^P) → Λ^k(ℝ^P) such that whenever IsUnitOrientationOf ξ Q: (a) |ξ(α)| ≤ |α| for every k-covector α; (b) |L(ξ)| ≤ 1; (c) ξ(L(ξ)) = 1.
- lusin_covector (Submission.dor_ims_lusin_continuousOn): for a measure ν on ℝ^P, a measurable A ⊆ ℝ^P with ν(A) < ∞, a ν-a.e. strongly measurable f : ℝ^P → Λ^k(ℝ^P) and a real η > 0, there is a compact K ⊆ A with ν(A ∖ K) < η such that f is continuous on K.
- smooth_unit_approximation (Submission.dor_ims_smooth_unit_approx): for K ⊆ G ⊆ ℝ^P with K compact and G open, β : ℝ^P → Λ^k(ℝ^P) continuous on K with |β(x)| ≤ 1 for x ∈ K, and δ > 0, there is a smooth compactly supported k-form ω₀ (IsTestForm ω₀) with tsupport ω₀ ⊆ G, |ω₀(x)| ≤ 1 for every x and |ω₀(x) − β(x)| ≤ δ for every x ∈ K.

Notation.
- H^k := μHE[k]; μ := H^k⌞M'; Λ^k := Covector (Euclid P) k with |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α; Λ_k := MultiVector P k.
- ν := μ with density ofReal∘θ', i.e. ν(B) = ∫⁻_B ofReal(θ') dμ = ∫⁻_{M'∩B} ofReal(θ') dH^k for Borel B (the second equality because (H^k⌞M')⌞B = H^k⌞(B ∩ M') for Borel B).
- I := I(W) = ∫⁻_{M'∩W} ofReal(θ') dH^k, assumed finite.
- ω ∈ 𝒟^k(U) is admissible for M_W(T) if tsupport ω ⊆ W and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for every x; by definition of the supremum, ofReal(T(ω)) ≤ M_W(T) for each admissible ω.

Proof. Fix the data and hypotheses of the statement and an open W ⊆ V with I < ∞.

1. (Good points.) Let L be the map of unit_orientation_dual for (P, k). Call x good if (a) |ξ'(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for every α ∈ Λ^k, (b) |L(ξ'(x))| ≤ 1 and (c) ξ'(x)(L(ξ'(x))) = 1. By the orientation hypothesis and unit_orientation_dual, μ-a.e. x is good. So the set of points that are not good is μ-null, and it is contained in a Borel set Z with μ(Z) = 0 (every null set has a measurable null superset).

2. (The measure ν.) ν ≪ μ, since ν(B) = ∫⁻_B ofReal(θ') dμ = 0 whenever μ(B) = 0. Hence ν(Z) = 0, and ν-a.e. x is good. W is open, hence Borel, so ν(W) = ∫⁻_W ofReal(θ') d(H^k⌞M') = ∫⁻_{M'∩W} ofReal(θ') dH^k = I < ∞, and ν(B) ≤ I for every Borel B ⊆ W. Write m := I, a real number ≥ 0.
 Density formula: ofReal∘θ' is measurable (θ' is) and finite everywhere, so every ν-integrable g : ℝ^P → ℝ satisfies ∫ g dν = ∫ (ofReal θ'(x)).toReal·g(x) dμ(x) = ∫ θ'·g dμ, because (ofReal θ'(x)).toReal = θ'(x) when θ'(x) ≥ 0 (Mathlib: integral_withDensity_eq_integral_toReal_smul).

3. (Reduction.) It suffices to prove r ≤ M_W(T) for every real r ≥ 0 with r < I; then I ≤ M_W(T) in [0, ∞]. Fix such an r, choose ε > 0 with r + ε < I, and put η := ε/4 > 0, so that r + 4η < m.

4. (Lusin.) h := L∘ξ' : ℝ^P → Λ^k is ν-a.e. strongly measurable: ξ' is μ-a.e. strongly measurable by hypothesis, hence ν-a.e. strongly measurable because ν ≪ μ, and L is continuous. The set A := W ∖ Z is Borel with ν(A) ≤ ν(W) < ∞. By lusin_covector, applied to ν, A, h and η, there is a compact K ⊆ A with ν(A ∖ K) < η such that h is continuous on K.
 (4a) K ⊆ W and K ∩ Z = ∅, so every x ∈ K is good; in particular |h(x)| ≤ 1 for x ∈ K, by (b).
 (4b) W ∖ K ⊆ (A ∖ K) ∪ Z, so ν(W ∖ K) ≤ ν(A ∖ K) + ν(Z) < η.
 (4c) K is compact, hence Borel, and K ⊆ W, so ν(K) + ν(W ∖ K) = ν(W) = m, all terms finite. With (4b), ν(K) > m − η; also ν(K) ≤ m.

5. (An admissible form.) Put δ := η/(m + 1) > 0. Apply smooth_unit_approximation to the compact set K, the open set G := W ⊇ K, β := h (continuous on K, with |β| ≤ 1 on K by (4a)) and δ. It gives a smooth compactly supported k-form ω₀ with tsupport ω₀ ⊆ W, |ω₀(x)| ≤ 1 for every x, and |ω₀(x) − h(x)| ≤ δ for every x ∈ K. Since tsupport ω₀ ⊆ W ⊆ V ⊆ U, ω₀ is an element ω of 𝒟^k(U), and ω is admissible for M_W(T). Hence ofReal(T(ω)) ≤ M_W(T).

6. (Integrability and the value of T(ω).) Let f(x) := ξ'(x)(ω₀(x)).
 - f is ν-a.e. strongly measurable: it is the composite of x ↦ (ξ'(x), ω₀(x)), which is ν-a.e. strongly measurable (ξ' by step 4, ω₀ continuous), with the evaluation pairing Λ_k × Λ^k → ℝ, (ζ, α) ↦ ζ(α), which is continuous (a bounded bilinear map).
 - For every good x, |f(x)| ≤ 1_W(x): if x ∉ W then x ∉ tsupport ω₀, so ω₀(x) = 0 and f(x) = 0; if x ∈ W then |f(x)| ≤ |ω₀(x)| ≤ 1 by (a).
 - 1_W is ν-integrable because ν(W) < ∞. Hence f is ν-integrable, and, by the representation hypothesis (tsupport ω ⊆ W ⊆ V) and the density formula of step 2,
 T(ω) = ∫_{M'} θ'(x)·ξ'(x)(ω₀(x)) dH^k(x) = ∫ θ'·f dμ = ∫ f dν.

7. (Pointwise lower bound.) For every good x,
 f(x) ≥ (1 − δ)·1_K(x) − 1_{W∖K}(x).
 - x ∈ K: by linearity of ξ'(x) and (c), f(x) = ξ'(x)(h(x)) + ξ'(x)(ω₀(x) − h(x)) = 1 + ξ'(x)(ω₀(x) − h(x)) ≥ 1 − |ω₀(x) − h(x)| ≥ 1 − δ, using (a).
 - x ∈ W ∖ K: f(x) ≥ −|ξ'(x)(ω₀(x))| ≥ −|ω₀(x)| ≥ −1, by (a).
 - x ∉ W: ω₀(x) = 0, so f(x) = 0, which is the value of the right side.
 Since ν-a.e. x is good, the inequality holds ν-a.e.

8. (Integration and arithmetic.) The right side of step 7 is ν-integrable (ν(K) and ν(W ∖ K) are finite), so monotonicity of the integral gives
 T(ω) = ∫ f dν ≥ (1 − δ)·ν(K) − ν(W ∖ K) = ν(K) − δ·ν(K) − ν(W ∖ K).
 Now δ·ν(K) ≤ δ·m = η·m/(m + 1) < η, ν(W ∖ K) < η by (4b), and ν(K) > m − η by (4c). Therefore
 T(ω) > (m − η) − η − η = m − 3η > (r + 4η) − 3η = r + η > r.

9. (Conclusion.) By steps 5 and 8, r = ofReal(r) ≤ ofReal(T(ω)) ≤ M_W(T). Since r ∈ [0, I) was arbitrary, I ≤ M_W(T). ∎
proof_key_steps: unit_orientation_dual gives L with |ξ'(α)| ≤ |α|, |L(ξ')| ≤ 1 and ξ'(L(ξ')) = 1 off a Borel H^k⌞M'-null set Z; ν := θ'·H^k⌞M' satisfies ν ≪ H^k⌞M' and ν(W) = I < ∞.
Reduce to r < I; with η = ε/4 and r + 4η < I, lusin_covector on A = W ∖ Z gives a compact K ⊆ A with ν(A ∖ K) < η on which L∘ξ' is continuous; since ν(Z) = 0, ν(W ∖ K) < η.
smooth_unit_approximation gives an admissible ω with tsupport ω ⊆ W, |ω| ≤ 1 and |ω − L∘ξ'| ≤ δ := η/(I + 1) on K.
T(ω) = ∫ ξ'(ω) dν ≥ (1 − δ)ν(K) − ν(W ∖ K) > I − 3η > r, so r ≤ M_W(T); hence I ≤ M_W(T).

(div φ is continuous with compact support, hence L-integrable on F.)

2. Mollification. Fix ρ ∈ C_c^∞(E) with ρ ≥ 0, ∫ρ = 1, spt ρ ⊆ B_1(0) (Mathlib `ContDiffBump.normed` for a bump centred at 0 with outer radius 1), and ρ_ε(x) := ε^{-(m+1)} ρ(x/ε). For g : E → E continuous with compact support put g_ε := ρ_ε * g (componentwise). Then g_ε is C^∞ (HasCompactSupport.contDiff_convolution_left); tsupport g_ε ⊆ (tsupport g)^ε; |g_ε(x)| ≤ ∫ρ_ε(x − z)|g(z)| dz ≤ ‖g‖_∞; and g_ε → g uniformly as ε ↓ 0 (g is uniformly continuous). If g is C¹, then D(g_ε) = ρ_ε * Dg, hence div g_ε = ρ_ε * div g → div g uniformly.

3. Extension. Let 𝒞 := {g : E → E continuous, compactly supported, tsupport g ⊆ D}. For g ∈ 𝒞, K := tsupport g and 0 < ε, ε′ < d_K, the field g_ε − g_{ε′} is C^∞ with tsupport in K^{d_K}, so by step 1 |∫_F div g_ε − ∫_F div g_{ε′}| ≤ C_{K^{d_K}} ‖g_ε − g_{ε′}‖_∞ → 0. Hence Λ(g) := −lim_{ε↓0} ∫_F div g_ε dL exists. Properties:
 (a) Λ is linear on 𝒞 (for g, h ∈ 𝒞 use the compact set tsupport g ∪ tsupport h; (g + h)_ε = g_ε + h_ε and (cg)_ε = c g_ε).
 (b) If g ∈ 𝒞 is C¹ then Λ(g) = −∫_F div g dL: div g_ε → div g uniformly and all these functions vanish outside the compact set K^{d_K}, of finite L-measure.
 (c) Local bound: if K ⊆ D is compact, g ∈ 𝒞, tsupport g ⊆ K and |g| ≤ 1, then |g_ε| ≤ 1 and tsupport g_ε ⊆ K^{d_K} for ε < d_K, so |Λ(g)| ≤ C_{K^{d_K}}.

4. Riesz representation on D. Regard D (an open subspace of E) as a locally compact Hausdorff space. For h ∈ C_c(D; E) its extension by zero h̃ lies in 𝒞: h̃ is continuous on the open set D and vanishes on the open set E \ tsupport_D h (a compact subset of D is closed in E), and these open sets cover E. Define L(h) := Λ(h̃); it is linear by 3(a), and for every compact K ⊆ D, L(h) ≤ C_{K^{d_K}} whenever |h| ≤ 1 and supp h ⊆ K, by 3(c). By Simon Ch. 1, 4.14 (X = D, H = E; SimonGMT `simon_theorem_4_14_caratheodory`) there are a Radon measure μ_D on D and a μ_D-measurable ν_D : D → E with |ν_D| = 1 μ_D-a.e. and L(h) = ∫_D ⟨h, ν_D⟩ dμ_D for all h ∈ C_c(D; E).

5. Transfer to E. Define the Borel measure μ(A) := μ_D(A ∩ D): the Borel restriction of the Carathéodory measure of μ_D (SimonGMT `opensMeasurableSpace_radonCaratheodoryMeasure`, `IsBorelRegularOuterMeasure.toBorelMeasure`) pushed forward along the inclusion D ↪ E. Then μ(E \ D) = 0 and μ(K) = μ_D(K) < ∞ for compact K ⊆ D. The Riesz field ν_D is measurable for the Carathéodory σ-algebra of μ_D; as μ_D is Borel regular and open σ-finite (D is σ-compact and μ_D is finite on compacts), each coordinate of ν_D is μ_D-a.e. equal to a Borel function (SimonGMT `IsBorelRegularOuterMeasure.aemeasurable_of_caratheodory`, applied coordinatewise; E is finite-dimensional). Hence ν_D agrees μ_D-a.e. with a Borel map ν₁ : E → E (on D), and integrals against the Carathéodory measure of μ_D and against μ coincide for such integrands. Fix a unit vector e ∈ E (E ≠ {0}) and set ν(y) := ν₁(y) if |ν₁(y)| = 1, ν(y) := e otherwise. Then ν is Borel, |ν(y)| = 1 for every y, and ν = ν_D μ-a.e. on D. Hence for g ∈ 𝒞: Λ(g) = L(g|_D) = ∫_D ⟨g, ν_D⟩ dμ_D = ∫_E ⟨g, ν⟩ dμ (the integrand is bounded and vanishes off the compact set tsupport g ⊆ D, which has finite μ-measure, so it is μ-integrable).

6. Gauss–Green. Let φ be C¹ with compact support and tsupport φ ⊆ D. Then φ ∈ 𝒞, and by 3(b) and step 5, −∫_F div φ dL = Λ(φ) = ∫⟨φ, ν⟩ dμ. With step 5 this gives every assertion: μ(E \ D) = 0, μ(K) < ∞ for compact K ⊆ D, ν Borel with |ν| ≡ 1, and ∫_F div φ dL = −∫⟨φ, ν⟩ dμ. ∎
proof_key_steps: Hypothesis applied to ±φ/sup|φ| gives |∫_F div φ| ≤ C_K sup|φ| for smooth φ supported in K.
Mollification gives smooth approximants supported in K^d with sup bound preserved and uniformly convergent divergence for C¹ fields.
Λ := −lim ∫_F div g_ε is a locally bounded linear functional on continuous compactly supported fields in D and equals −∫_F div g on C¹ fields.
Simon Ch. 1, 4.14 on the locally compact space D yields a Radon μ_D and a unit polar field ν_D.
Push μ_D forward to ℝ^{m+1}; take a Borel representative of ν_D and make it unit everywhere.
Gauss–Green identity for C¹ fields from 3(b) and the representation.

subproblems.title: Identification μ = H^m⌞B with approximate tangent planes ν^⊥, given rectifiable density one (Simon 4.3 first part) (reused accepted codim1_rdo_dg_measure_eq_hausdorff)
subproblems.statement: Let m ≥ 1, let D ⊆ ℝ^{m+1} be open, μ a Borel measure on ℝ^{m+1} with μ(ℝ^{m+1} \ D) = 0 and μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ D, and ν : ℝ^{m+1} → ℝ^{m+1} Borel with |ν(y)| = 1 for every y. Assume that for μ-a.e. y and every continuous compactly supported f : ℝ^{m+1} → ℝ, r^{-m} ∫ f(r^{-1}(z − y)) dμ(z) → ∫_{(span{ν(y)})^⊥} f dH^m as r ↓ 0 (H^m = μHE[m]). Assume also (RD): for every Borel countably m-rectifiable S ⊆ ℝ^{m+1} with H^m(S) < ∞, H^m(S ∩ B_t(w))/(ω_m t^m) → 1 as t ↓ 0 for H^m-a.e. w ∈ S (ω_m = unitBallVolume m). Then there is a Borel, countably m-rectifiable B ⊆ D with μ = H^m⌞B (as measures) such that for H^m-a.e. y ∈ B the approximate tangent space of B at y (Simon Ch. 3, 1.4) is (span{ν(y)})^⊥.

Reuse. This child is the comparator-accepted declaration codim1_rdo_dg_measure_eq_hausdorff (DAG node root.dimension_reduction_results-a1.codimension_one_regularity-a1.region_density_one-a1.de_giorgi-a1.hausdorff_identification-a1, status accepted, accepted candidate commit 3632b244600d917333b1ceef4709c265614d91ef; isolated comparator passed). It is reused with its identical frozen type: a whitespace-normalised comparison with the declaration in that commit matches. That commit's GMT/Ch07/Contract.lean is byte-identical to the frozen contract, its only sorry is the frozen root theorem, and it declares no axioms. Role here: It is used by de_giorgi (step 5). From the flat tangent measures of the Gauss–Green measure μ at μ-a.e. point (de_giorgi step 4(f)) and the density theorem (RD) supplied by rect_density_one, it gives a Borel countably n-rectifiable B with μ = H^n⌞B and approximate tangent planes ν^⊥. This replaces v1's instruction to adapt the printed proof of Ch. 3, 1.6: the measure-level rectifiability argument (uniform density/cone estimates, cone exclusion, Lipschitz graphs, countable covering) is in the accepted proof of the rectifiable_criterion cited below. Its accepted proof cites the accepted declarations codim1_rdo_dg_flat_tangent_density_cone and codim1_rdo_dg_rectifiable_of_flat_tangent of its original decomposition (as flat_tangent_density and rectifiable_criterion); both are contained in the same candidate commit, so they create no obligation here. The proof below is the accepted proof of this declaration, copied verbatim.

Source. Expansion of the printed first sentence of the proof of Simon Ch. 3, 4.3 ("By 1.6 and 3.6 of Ch. 1, the first part of the theorem follows from 4.3(†)", chapter-03.txt line 604), exactly as in parent proof steps 5, 7 and 8: comparison of μ with H^m (Ch. 1, 3.2–3.4, chapter-01.txt lines 578–640), Radon–Nikodym differentiation (Ch. 1, 3.23–3.24, lines 1063–1180; Mathlib `Besicovitch.ae_tendsto_rnDeriv`), the rectifiable density theorem (hypothesis (RD); in the parent it is supplied by the sibling rectifiable_density_one, `Submission.codim1_rdo_rectifiable_ae_density_one` with P := m + 1, n := m), and Definition 1.4 of Ch. 3 (chapter-03.txt lines 80–90). Dependencies: flat_tangent_density, rectifiable_criterion.

Notation. E := ℝ^{m+1}; H^m := μHE[m] = κ_m·μH[m] for a constant κ_m ∈ (0, ∞) (definition of μHE); ω_m := unitBallVolume m; P_y := (span{ν(y)})^⊥; G := {y ∈ D : the flat-tangent convergence holds at y}, so μ(E \ G) = 0.

1. Density of μ. For y ∈ G some B̄_{r₀}(y) ⊆ D (D open) has finite μ-measure, so flat_tangent_density gives μ(B̄_r(y))/(ω_m r^m) → 1 and μ(B_r(y))/(ω_m r^m) → 1 as r ↓ 0.

2. Carrier. rectifiable_criterion gives a Borel countably m-rectifiable R with μ(E \ R) = 0. Let N := toMeasurable μ (E \ G) (Borel, N ⊇ E \ G, μ(N) = 0) and B := (D ∩ R) \ N. Then B is Borel, B ⊆ D, B ⊆ R ∩ G, B is countably m-rectifiable (`CountablyRectifiable.mono`), and μ(E \ B) ≤ μ(E \ D) + μ(E \ R) + μ(N) = 0. Let λ := μHE[m].restrict B.

3. Local finiteness of λ (comparison of Ch. 1, 3.3 type). Claim: H^m(B ∩ V) ≤ c_m μ(V) for every open V with V̄ compact ⊆ D, where c_m := 2·10^m κ_m/ω_m. Fix θ > 0. Every x ∈ B ∩ V lies in G, so by step 1 there are arbitrarily small r ∈ (0, θ/10) with B̄_r(x) ⊆ V and μ(B̄_r(x)) ≥ ½ ω_m r^m. By the 5r-covering lemma (Ch. 1, 3.4; Mathlib `Vitali.exists_disjoint_subfamily_covering_enlargement_closedBall`) there is a disjoint subfamily B̄_{r_i}(x_i), countable because each member has positive μ-measure and μ(V) < ∞, with B ∩ V ⊆ ⋃_i B̄_{5r_i}(x_i). As diam B̄_{5r_i}(x_i) ≤ 10 r_i < θ, the θ-approximation of μH[m] satisfies μH[m]_θ(B ∩ V) ≤ Σ_i (10 r_i)^m ≤ (2·10^m/ω_m) Σ_i μ(B̄_{r_i}(x_i)) ≤ (2·10^m/ω_m) μ(V). Letting θ ↓ 0 and multiplying by κ_m proves the claim. Consequently H^m(B ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ D (take an open V ⊇ K with V̄ compact ⊆ D).

4. μ ≪ λ (parent step 5(b)). Let A ⊆ B with H^m(A) = 0. For k ≥ 1 let A_k := {x ∈ A : μ(B̄_r(x)) ≤ 2 ω_m r^m for all r ∈ (0, 1/k)}; by step 1, A = ⋃_k A_k. Fix k, η > 0 and 0 < θ < 1/k. Since μH[m](A_k) = 0, there is a countable cover of A_k by sets C_i with diam C_i < θ and Σ_i (diam C_i)^m < η; discard the C_i not meeting A_k and pick a_i ∈ C_i ∩ A_k. Then C_i ⊆ B̄_{diam C_i}(a_i) and μ(B̄_{diam C_i}(a_i)) ≤ 2 ω_m (diam C_i)^m (if diam C_i = 0, then μ({a_i}) ≤ 2 ω_m r^m for all small r > 0, so it is 0). Hence μ(A_k) ≤ 2 ω_m η, so μ(A_k) = 0 and μ(A) = 0. Therefore, for Borel A with λ(A) = H^m(A ∩ B) = 0: μ(A) = μ(A ∩ B) = 0, i.e. μ ≪ λ.

5. Density of λ. Let W be an open ball with W̄ ⊆ D and S := B ∩ W: Borel, countably m-rectifiable, H^m(S) < ∞ by step 3. By (RD), for H^m-a.e. w ∈ S, H^m(S ∩ B_t(w))/(ω_m t^m) → 1; for w ∈ W and t < dist(w, E \ W), S ∩ B_t(w) = B ∩ B_t(w). As D is a countable union of such balls and λ(E \ D) = 0, λ(B_t(w))/(ω_m t^m) → 1 for λ-a.e. w. Since B_t(w) ⊆ B̄_t(w) ⊆ B_{t(1+ε)}(w) for every ε > 0, also λ(B̄_t(w))/(ω_m t^m) → 1 for λ-a.e. w.

6. Identification μ = λ (parent step 7, "θ = 1"). Let W be an open ball with W̄ ⊆ D, μ_W := μ⌞W and λ_W := λ⌞W: finite Borel measures with μ_W ≪ λ_W (step 4). By Besicovitch differentiation (Mathlib `Besicovitch.ae_tendsto_rnDeriv`), for λ_W-a.e. w, μ_W(B̄_t(w))/λ_W(B̄_t(w)) → (dμ_W/dλ_W)(w) as t ↓ 0. For λ-a.e. w ∈ W we have w ∈ B ⊆ G, and for small t (B̄_t(w) ⊆ W) steps 1 and 5 give μ_W(B̄_t(w))/λ_W(B̄_t(w)) = [μ(B̄_t(w))/(ω_m t^m)]/[λ(B̄_t(w))/(ω_m t^m)] → 1. Hence dμ_W/dλ_W = 1 λ_W-a.e., and by Radon–Nikodym (μ_W ≪ λ_W; Mathlib `withDensity_rnDeriv_eq`) μ_W = λ_W. Covering D by countably many such balls W_l (disjointified as W_l \ ⋃_{i<l} W_i) and using μ(E \ D) = λ(E \ D) = 0, μ(A) = λ(A) for every Borel A: μ = μHE[m].restrict B.

7. Approximate tangent planes (parent step 8; Definition 1.4). Let y ∈ B, so y ∈ G. P_y is the orthogonal complement of a line in ℝ^{m+1}, so finrank P_y = m. For r > 0, η_r(z) := r^{-1}(z − y) (Simon's η_{y,r}; SimonGMT `blowUpMap y r`) is a bijective similarity with ratio r^{-1}, so μHE[m](η_r(A)) = r^{-m} μHE[m](A) for every A (translation invariance and Mathlib `euclideanHausdorffMeasure_smul₀`); hence μHE[m]⌞η_r(B) = r^{-m} (η_r)_#(μHE[m]⌞B), and for every f ∈ C_c(E; ℝ),
 ∫_{η_r(B)} f dH^m = r^{-m} ∫_B f(η_r(z)) dH^m(z) = r^{-m} ∫ f(r^{-1}(z − y)) dμ(z) → ∫_{P_y} f dH^m (y ∈ G and step 6).
 Thus HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt m B y P_y holds for every y ∈ B, in particular for λ-a.e. y. Together with steps 2 and 6, B is Borel, B ⊆ D, countably m-rectifiable, and μ = μHE[m].restrict B. ∎
proof_key_steps: Flat tangents give Θ^m(μ,y) = 1 on G (flat_tangent_density).
Carrier B = (D ∩ R) ∖ N ⊆ G, rectifiable by rectifiable_criterion, of full μ-measure.
Vitali 5r-covering: H^m⌞B ≤ c_m μ locally, so H^m⌞B is locally finite.
Covering argument: H^m-null subsets of B are μ-null, so μ ≪ H^m⌞B.
(RD) gives density one of H^m⌞B a.e.; Besicovitch differentiation gives dμ/dλ = 1, hence μ = H^m⌞B.
Scaling of H^m under η_{y,r} turns the flat tangent measure into HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt with plane ν(y)^⊥.

Reuse. This child is the comparator-accepted declaration codim1_rdo_rectifiable_ae_density_one (DAG node root.dimension_reduction_results-a1.codimension_one_regularity-a1.region_density_one-a1.rectifiable_density_one-a1, status accepted, accepted candidate commit be5e5124bcc122be14e4b41214ce012bae5b1691; isolated comparator passed). It is reused with its identical frozen type: a whitespace-normalised comparison with the declaration in that commit matches. That commit's GMT/Ch07/Contract.lean is byte-identical to the frozen contract, its only sorry is the frozen root theorem, and it declares no axioms. Role here: Its instance P := n + 1 is exactly hypothesis (RD) of measure_eq_hausdorff, as used in de_giorgi (step 5). Its accepted proof cites the accepted declarations regcomp_atl_upper_density_zero, rsd_tendsto_closedBall_density_of_approxTangent and rsd_tendsto_ball_density_of_closedBall; they are contained in the same candidate commit, so they create no obligation here. The proof below is the accepted proof of this declaration, copied verbatim.

Source. General fact (G7) of the supplied proof, cited there from Simon Ch. 3, 1.8(2) and 1.9. For a set of finite H^n-measure (multiplicity θ ≡ 1) these reduce to the following printed items, copied here with the omitted details supplied:
- Lemma 1.2, ‘only if’ (chapter-03.txt lines 25–66);
- Remark 1.3 (lines 67–76);
- the proof of Theorem 1.6 ‘⇒’ (lines 109–144);
- Remark 1.5(3) (lines 91–100).

Notation.
- H^n = μHE[n]. It is isometry invariant, H^n(λA) = λ^n H^n(A), and it equals Lebesgue measure L^n on ℝ^n and on n-planes.
- ω_n = unitBallVolume n.
- η_{w,r}(z) = r^{-1}(z − w) (SimonGMT blowUpMap).
- An n-dimensional subspace Q is an approximate tangent space of M at w (Simon Ch. 3, 1.4; HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M w Q) if ∫_{η_{w,r}(M)} f dH^n → ∫_Q f dH^n as r ↓ 0, for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P).

Proof.
1. (Lemma 1.2, ‘only if’: a C¹ cover.)
- By countable n-rectifiability, M ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_{j≥1} F_j(ℝ^n) with H^n(M₀) = 0 and F_j : ℝ^n → ℝ^P Lipschitz.
- Fix j. Apply the C¹ Approximation Theorem (Simon Ch. 2, 1.5; chapter-02.txt line 165) to the P coordinates of F_j. For each i ≥ 1 this gives a C¹ map G_{ij} : ℝ^n → ℝ^P with L^n({F_j ≠ G_{ij}}) < 1/i.
- Put Z_j := ℝ^n ∖ ⋃_i {F_j = G_{ij}}. Then L^n(Z_j) ≤ 1/i for every i, so L^n(Z_j) = 0. E_j := F_j(Z_j) satisfies H^n(E_j) ≤ Lip(F_j)^n L^n(Z_j) = 0. Thus F_j(ℝ^n) ⊆ E_j ∪ ⋃_i G_{ij}(ℝ^n).
- Let C_{ij} := {z : DG_{ij}(z) not injective}, a closed set on which the Jacobian J_{G_{ij}} vanishes. By the area formula for C¹ (locally Lipschitz) maps (Simon Ch. 2, §3: ∫ H⁰(A ∩ G^{-1}(y)) dH^n(y) = ∫_A J_G dL^n; cf. SimonGMT Chapter02/AreaCritical), H^n(G_{ij}(C_{ij})) = 0.
- Let z ∉ C_{ij}. Apply the inverse function theorem to G_{ij} followed by the orthogonal projection onto DG_{ij}(z)(ℝ^n). This gives an open ball B_z ∋ z, with closure in ℝ^n ∖ C_{ij}, such that G_{ij} is a C¹ embedding near closure B_z: injective, a homeomorphism onto its image, with injective derivative. Moreover H^n(G_{ij}(B_z)) ≤ Lip(G_{ij}|closure B_z)^n L^n(B_z) < ∞.
- By Lindelöf, countably many such balls cover ℝ^n ∖ C_{ij}.
- Altogether M ⊆ N₀ ∪ ⋃_{k≥1} N_k, where N₀ := M₀ ∪ ⋃_j E_j ∪ ⋃_{i,j} G_{ij}(C_{ij}) is H^n-null. Each N_k = g_k(B_k) is the image of an open ball under a C¹ embedding g_k defined near closure B_k, is σ-compact (hence Borel), and has H^n(N_k) < ∞.
2. (Remark 1.3.) Put M_k := (M ∩ N_k) ∖ ⋃_{1≤i<k} N_i for k ≥ 1. These are pairwise disjoint Borel sets with M_k ⊆ N_k, and M ∖ ⋃_k M_k ⊆ N₀ is H^n-null.
3. (Tangent planes of the C¹ pieces.) Fix k and w = g_k(z) ∈ N_k, and let T_wN_k := Dg_k(z)(ℝ^n), an n-dimensional subspace.
- g_k is a homeomorphism of B_k onto N_k with injective derivative at z. So there are ρ₀, c, s > 0 with |g_k(z′) − w| ≥ c|z′ − z| for z′ ∈ B_{ρ₀}(z) ⊆ B_k, and N_k ∩ B_s(w) ⊆ g_k(B_{ρ₀}(z)).
- Let f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P) vanish outside B_R(0) and let r < s/R. By the area formula and the substitution z′ = z + ra, ∫_{η_{w,r}(N_k)} f dH^n = ∫ f(r^{-1}(g_k(z + ra) − w))·J_{g_k}(z + ra) dL^n(a). The integrand vanishes for |a| > R/c.
- As r ↓ 0, r^{-1}(g_k(z + ra) − w) → Dg_k(z)a uniformly for |a| ≤ R/c, and J_{g_k}(z + ra) → J_{g_k}(z). By dominated convergence the integral tends to ∫ f(Dg_k(z)a) J_{g_k}(z) da = ∫_{T_wN_k} f dH^n (area formula for the linear map Dg_k(z)).
4. (Proof of Theorem 1.6 ‘⇒’.) Fix k ≥ 1, f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P) with f = 0 outside B_R(0), w ∈ M_k and r > 0. Since M = M_k ⊔ (M ∖ M_k) and N_k = M_k ⊔ (N_k ∖ M_k),
 ∫_{η_{w,r}(M)} f dH^n = ∫_{η_{w,r}(N_k)} f dH^n − ∫_{η_{w,r}(N_k∖M_k)} f dH^n + ∫_{η_{w,r}(M∖M_k)} f dH^n.
- By step 3 the first term tends to ∫_{T_wN_k} f dH^n.
- For Borel A with H^n(A) < ∞: |∫_{η_{w,r}(A)} f dH^n| ≤ sup|f|·r^{-n}H^n(A ∩ B_{rR}(w)) = sup|f|·R^n(rR)^{-n}H^n(A ∩ B_{rR}(w)).
